newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - opens quiet, under pressure.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - opens quiet, under pressure.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds opened Monday morning in quiet trade, off about 1/8 in the cash market, with concern mounting about this week's supply and economic data.

"It is quiet, a touch negative," said one Wall Street muni trader. "It's a bit on the bear side," he added, noting a variety of causes, including the sales calendar, a lack of business and inventories.
Another trader said the market was "very quiet, unchanged to off 1/8."
While he said he welcomed supply this weeek, about $2.4 billion in muni sales are expected, he expressed concern about the data slated for release this week.
"We have a barrage of economic indicators," he said. "We are under a little bit of pressure."
Municipal bond sales for this week are expected to total $2.4 billion in 88 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $2 billion in 37 sales, with a $640 million NYC Municipal Water Agency deal through J.P. Morgan Securities Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 51 sales totaling $453 million are on the schedule. A $115 million Montgomery County, Md., deal on Tuesday is the largest.
An additional 11 sales totaling $570 million are on the possible calender, meaning underwriters have said they may price the bonds this week, depending on market conditions.
In the U.S. government cash market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 5/32 at 93-15/32 to yield 7.16 percent.
In debt futures the June Municipal contract was off 3/32 at 112-4/32. The June T-bond contract was down 4/32 at 107.
The MOB spread was 164 ticks, up from Friday's close of 163 ticks.
